questions.stem: Why is bioethanol considered a renewable fuel?

options.text: It comes from crude oil which is constantly forming
It is made from plants that can be regrown, and the CO2 released when burned is absorbed by the next crop
It never runs out because it is recycled from exhaust gases
It is made from nuclear reactions

questions.explanation: Bioethanol is renewable because it is made by fermenting sugars from plants (such as sugar cane or corn) that can be replanted and regrown. The carbon cycle means CO2 released during combustion is reabsorbed by the next crop during photosynthesis, making it approximately carbon neutral.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of hydrogen as a fuel?

options.text: It is easy to store and transport
The only product of its combustion is water, so it produces no CO2 emissions
It is the cheapest fuel available
It is found in large underground reserves

questions.explanation: The main advantage of hydrogen is that burning it produces only water: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O. There are no CO2 emissions when hydrogen is used. However, challenges include storage (hydrogen is very light and needs compression), the energy required for production, and the need for new infrastructure.
